parsed.summary: The Lean file proves two lower bounds on the number of variable leaves of a formula over ℂ that computes the n×n permanent, for n ≥ 32. A division-free formula needs at least n⁴/(128·log₂ n) variable leaves. A valid formula with division, evaluated in the fraction field of ℂ[x_ij] with every denominator nonzero, needs at least n⁴/(192·log₂ n). These match the L_var parts of Theorems 1.2 and 1.3. The main caveat is coverage: the gate-count bounds G(Φ), the circuit bound of Theorem 1.1, and the total-leaf/vertex variants are not formalized.

The polynomial in R[x_i] computed by the formula.
Number of leaves labeled by variables, counting repeated occurrences separately: L_var(Φ).

glossary.note: Division by zero would return the junk value 0, but Valid excludes it.

glossary.plain: Every ÷ gate has a denominator that evaluates to a nonzero rational function; checked recursively over all subformulas.

lean_claims.plain: For n ≥ 32 and any division-free formula f over ℂ in the variables x_ij whose evaluation equals per_n: n⁴/(128·log₂ n) ≤ L_var(f).
For n ≥ 32 and any valid formula f with division over ℂ whose value in ℂ(x_ij) equals per_n: n⁴/(192·log₂ n) ≤ L_var(f).

paper_claims.plain: For n ≥ 32 and a division-free formula Φ computing per_n: L_var(Φ) ≥ n⁴/(128 log₂ n) and G(Φ) ≥ n⁴/(256 log₂ n); the leaf bound also holds for total leaves and vertices.
For n ≥ 32 and a valid formula Φ with division computing per_n: L_var(Φ) ≥ n⁴/(192 log₂ n) and G(Φ) ≥ n⁴/(384 log₂ n); the leaf bound also holds for total leaves and vertices.
